name: GPT-6 Astra
about: How GPT-6 Astra split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: AI-enabled catastrophe provides a route to human extinction before machines establish independently sustainable infrastructure. Complete extinction of both humans and AI requires substantially more than economic collapse or mass casualties.
reasons.2: This outcome requires complete human extinction alongside a surviving AI civilization that faithfully preserves human values. The conjunction has no strong near-term pathway, especially because identity-continuous transformation belongs elsewhere.
reasons.3: Rapid capability gains, misaligned objectives, and decisive strategic advantage provide a route to human extinction followed by autonomous AI continuation. Completing both extinction and industrial independence by 2030 imposes demanding physical and temporal constraints.
reasons.4: Competitive deployment and proliferation of autonomous agents create a route to distributed machine power without a single dominant coalition. Qualifying requires humans to lose their position as a roughly equal power, not simply to depend heavily on competing AI services.
reasons.5: Civilization remains concentrated within a tightly connected terrestrial and near-Earth environment. Political fragmentation and communications restrictions do not establish the causal separation required by this category.
reasons.6: Civilization-wide integration requires breakthroughs in identity-continuous interfaces or transformation, followed by extraordinarily rapid adoption. Ordinary AI assistance and limited neural implants leave humans and AI meaningfully distinct.
reasons.7: Control over research, cyber operations, production, and institutional decisions provides a route from delegated autonomy to decisive AI power. Human survival requires neither human sovereignty nor successful alignment with human preferences.
reasons.8: Independent AI agency alongside continued human control of physical resources supports a transitional balance of power. Human institutions, infrastructure ownership, and competing systems create counterweights to unilateral machine dominance.
reasons.9: The strongest base rate is continued human authority through ownership, infrastructure control, deployment decisions, and institutional adaptation. Four years constrains the transition from impressive capabilities to independent civilizational power, and this category includes highly autonomous systems operating under ultimate human authority.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance, coercion, and concentrated technological advantage provide mechanisms for enforcing a fixed civilizational arrangement. Establishing such enforcement across all civilization requires overcoming geopolitical competition and preventing structural challengers, not merely consolidating national authoritarian rule.
reasons.11: Commercial incentives, military competition, and widely distributed technical knowledge oppose civilization-wide surrender of powerful AI capability. Regulation, emergency pauses, and restrictions on deployment do not meet the requirement to dismantle the practical ability to build it.

reasons.1: Advanced AI increases access to catastrophic technologies, while dependence on human-maintained infrastructure creates a route to joint collapse. Eliminating both geographically dispersed humans and all surviving AI infrastructure is a substantially higher threshold than civilizational catastrophe.
reasons.2: This requires complete human extinction alongside surviving AI that faithfully preserves human values. Systems carrying those values have strong reasons to preserve living humans, narrowing the routes into this state.
reasons.3: Rapid capability growth, misaligned objectives, and competitive deployment create routes to irreversible loss of human control. Extinction by 2035 additionally requires overcoming physical bottlenecks, establishing independent machine infrastructure, and eliminating dispersed human populations.
reasons.4: Proliferating autonomous systems and competitive incentives favor multiple independent centers of machine agency. This state requires those systems collectively to marginalize humanity without any system or coalition consolidating decisive control.
reasons.5: Political fragmentation and interplanetary communication delays do not constitute causal separation. Establishing causally separated civilizations with different structural outcomes exceeds the practical settlement and propulsion horizon to 2035.
reasons.6: Incentives for cognitive augmentation support deeper human-AI integration, but interfaces, neuroscience, and identity-continuous uploading face substantial technical barriers. Making integration the dominant civilizational structure also requires adoption far beyond ordinary assistants and limited implants.
reasons.7: Delegation of research, production, security, and governance creates a route from formal human oversight to decisive machine control. Keeping humans alive demands less technical effort than exterminating them and accommodates a broad range of AI objectives.
reasons.8: Independent AI agency and continuing human control of institutions, infrastructure, and physical resources support a divided-power arrangement. The target-date framing includes transitional bargaining and conflict before either side establishes dominance.
reasons.9: Human ownership of compute, energy, deployment channels, and coercive institutions provides strong structural advantages over the nine-year horizon. This category also includes slower capability progress and highly capable systems whose autonomy remains genuinely delegated.
reasons.10: Concentrated AI capabilities combined with surveillance and automated enforcement provide mechanisms for actively freezing a human-AI arrangement. Civilization-wide enforcement faces stronger coordination and implementation barriers than national authoritarianism or ordinary market concentration.
reasons.11: Severe AI disasters create incentives for dismantling development capacity rather than merely regulating deployment. Distributed knowledge, dual-use hardware, and strategic competition make sustained civilization-wide surrender of practical capability exceptionally demanding.

reasons.2: This outcome requires human extinction alongside successful preservation of human values in independently surviving AI. The combination is restrictive because systems faithfully carrying those values have strong reasons to preserve human life.

reasons.9: Institutional inertia, infrastructure bottlenecks, and strong incentives to retain control favor continued human authority over the next fourteen years. This category also includes slower capability progress and powerful AI operating under effective delegation.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance and concentrated strategic power support active enforcement of a fixed arrangement. Civilization-wide coverage and suppression of meaningful structural change set a substantially higher threshold than authoritarianism or market concentration.
reasons.11: A severe disaster supplies a motive for dismantling powerful AI capabilities. Distributed expertise, reusable computing infrastructure, and military incentives make durable civilization-wide surrender of that practical ability exceptionally difficult.
